doc.title: Charlie Gabriel interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 9, 2020

chapter: New Orleans funerals and early working life
title: Who paid the musicians for funerals
summary: Questions about band leader contracts and whether the family of the deceased pays; the ritual was already old when he arrived.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Who was responsible for paying the musicians?
Who would be responsible for paying the musicians?
Well he’d have a contract. For the funeral or something like that?
Well I would state he had a contract, but someone gives him X amount of dollars to take care of the person that you are using. But I never had a job myself as the band leader to play a funeral.
I just was curious if the family of the deceased —

It probably is the family of the deceased. Well they still pay for funerals and things. And they also not only pay for the funeral, when they take them to the different churches they give the people in the church money too sometimes you know. Because the only people that come to see the loved one that has gone, they’re still sad but they’re so thankful you’ve been so nice to them during that period of time through their mourning and

everything else. It’s a beautiful thing. It’s a ritual that we’ve been — it kind of opened my eyes up when they were doing this, so I imagine they were doing it for a long time before I opened my eyes up, because those were older guys, older musicians, and it didn’t happen just when I come into the world, it was already going on. I just followed the path.
